questions.stem: How is a tipping point used in sensitivity analysis?

answer.exemplar: It quantifies how much unobserved confounding would be needed to change the conclusion, helping readers assess robustness.

questions.explanation: It quantifies required unobserved confounding. Readers use it to assess robustness.

questions.subject: STATISTICS
questions.topic: Why a preregistered plan that changes is exploratory
questions.learningObjective: Explain when a deviation is acceptable
questions.stem: A preregistered plan is changed due to a data anomaly; what is the best practice?

options.text: Discard all data after the deviation
Hide the deviation to preserve credibility
Document and justify the deviation transparently

questions.explanation: Transparent documentation and justification is best. Hiding or fabricating plans undermines credibility.
